lisa_customer: Hey team — our prod service started returning a bunch of 429s around 10:02 UTC. It looks correlated to a per-minute cron that fires for many tenants. ~30% of calls failing for ~2 minutes. Customers hitting timeouts. Any quick triage steps?

sara_support: Sorry about that — can you paste one of the failing response headers (X-RateLimit-*) and the client retry/concurrency settings? That'll help narrow RPM vs TPM.

lisa_customer: Sample response via curl: 

HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1200
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1678900000
Retry-After: 30

Client: node SDK v2.3, default retries (3), no jitter, cron spawns 50 workers at once.

throttle-bot: Automated alert: rate_limit_reached tenant_id=acme-ops rpm=1200 tpm=20000 window=60s

nate_reliability: Pattern matches a minute-boundary fanout plus synchronized cron. Two common amplifiers: (1) many clients firing at the same second (minute boundary), (2) aggressive retries without randomized backoff causing retrystorms.

jordan_sre: Quick repro you can run locally to see the effect: 

# simulate 200 requests in parallel for 90s
seq 1 200 | xargs -n1 -P50 -I{} curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate\"

This will show a spike of 429s if RPM cap is hit.

sara_support: Short-term mitigations:
- Add jitter to cron start times (randomize within +-30s) to avoid minute alignment.
- Implement exponential backoff with jitter for retries (e.g., base=200ms, factor=2, cap=10s).
- Reduce concurrent worker count temporarily.
- If you need immediate relief we can request a temporary quota bump; we do that while you roll out fixes.

Longer-term: consider request batching, streaming (to reduce per-request token overhead), or Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput.

lisa_customer: Thanks — we'll push jitter + cap retries now. Can you open a temp bump request while we deploy?

sara_support: Filed INC-8421 for a one-off RPM increase and added logs to the ticket. Someone from infra will follow up in the hour. (thumbsup by nate_reliability)

nate_reliability: Also check client HTTP/2 multiplexing — if you have many logical streams that can still create mini-spikes. If you can, limit per-process concurrency to smooth token refill.

lisa_customer: Got it. I'll update you once we roll the jitter and monitor. Thanks all. :pray:
